article_framing_rejections.headline: U.S. Marshals arrest father of 3-month-old who died from malnutrition in Fort Pierce

lead_independence.headline: U.S. Marshals arrest father of 3-month-old who died from malnutrition in Fort Pierce
lead_independence.lead: U.S. Marshals Service arrested Jason Gunter, 45, Tuesday at his home in Mechanicsville, Virginia, on an outstanding warrant obtained by St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office detectives. Gunter, the biological father of 3-month-old Robert Gunter, has been charged with felony child neglect causing great bodily harm and is awaiting extradition to St. Lucie County. The arrest comes after three others were previously charged in the case: the child's mother, 27-year-old Nicole Maxwell; the child's grandfather, Robert Maxwell; and Robert Maxwell's girlfriend, 38-year-old Vikki Koon. All three were charged with aggravated manslaughter of a child and aggravated child abuse, each held on a $1.5 million bond.

lead_independence.headline: St. Lucie County prosecutors seek bail hearing for woman charged in Southern Truss fraud case
lead_independence.lead: Prosecutors have asked a judge to hold a hearing on the legitimacy and source of any bail premium or collateral before allowing Laura Beth Grasso to be released from the St. Lucie County Jail, arguing in a court filing that a defendant should not be able to use money obtained through criminal activity to secure her release. Grasso was arrested July 16 along with Sheri Lynn Harrs and Tina Marie Mejia following what the sheriff's office described as a years-long scheme targeting Southern Truss Companies. Grasso has pleaded not guilty to the charges, court records show.

article_framing_rejections.headline: Search warrant executed at Fort Pierce home in Southern Truss fraud case

lead_independence.headline: Search warrant executed at Fort Pierce home in Southern Truss fraud case
lead_independence.lead: Deputies executed a search warrant Tuesday morning at the Indian River Estates home of Laura Beth Grasso near Sunset Boulevard. Grasso was arrested July 16 along with Sheri Lynn Harrs and Tina Marie Mejia following what the sheriff's office described as a years-long scheme targeting Southern Truss Companies. Grasso has pleaded not guilty to the charges. Investigators allege Grasso, who worked as the company's bookkeeper and comptroller, used her administrative access to bypass financial controls and funnel millions of dollars out of the business. Detectives say the money was spent on luxury vehicles, vacations, designer goods, jewelry and other personal expenses.

lead_independence.headline: Tradition Lakes K-8 prepares to open in St. Lucie County
lead_independence.lead: Crews have worked throughout the summer to prepare the campus for its first group of students. Principal Latanya Greene said the school's motto, 'Traditions begin here,' reflects the focus on building a foundation of achievements and accomplishments. Greene emphasized that months of planning have gone into creating an environment where students can grow academically and socially. 'It's about being in an environment that you can grow and continue with great levels. But bigger than that, you begin to set the tone of creating those strong academics that move with you from year to year to year. You develop friendships,' Greene said.
